boardSettings: Timezone set from Asia/Shanghai to Asia/Hong_Kong (same UTC+8 clock). Duolingo's China check keys on Asia/Shanghai/Chongqing/Urumqi; with them it showed only a +86 phone and email login. The batch targets Hong Kong apps.

launch.evidence: Welcome screen rendered on the dedicated host and on v25.

google_sign_in.evidence: Sign in -> Google -> Play services' chooser (Choose an account to continue to Duolingo) listed the test account; selecting it returned OAuth and ID tokens through the broker and Duolingo's server answered with the account: 'There is no Duolingo profile for that Google account'. The first try was refused locally (client_id_not_granted): Duolingo requests the project-number client ID (<number>.apps.googleusercontent.com), not its default_web_client_id; the grant now names that ID.

google_sign_up.gap: Profile creation follows onboarding and a first lesson. Starting the lesson crashed the app: SIGSEGV in librive-android.so (Rive runtime, worker thread) at file offset 0x48c138, a 16-byte load from a null-based array (address -112) in a loop over 112-byte records. Not an EGL or GL call; cause open. The OH crash dump's backtrace offsets are 0x31000 too high (the faulting map gives 0x48c138).

onboarding.evidence: Course choice, source, level, reason, daily goal, reminder prompt (declined) and the course download all worked.

facebook_sign_in.gap: Facebook -> FacebookActivity (no Facebook app) -> CustomTabMainActivity -> Facebook's web login (m.facebook.com) rendered in Westlake's in-app web view. Focusing the email field crashed the app twice with SIGTRAP inside the in-process Chromium (Chrome_InProcRendererThread; once ThreadPoolForeground), before any credential was submitted. Same crash class as FotMob's earlier Chrome-thread trap; cause open.

otherGaps: Plain taps (tap channel 'i') reach the window but no view takes them (down=0 up=0); the main-queue click ('c') works.
Duolingo's widget prompt calls appwidget.requestPinAppWidget; Westlake answers every call with defaults and no pin result follows, so the 'I'm in' screen needs a second tap.
One start aborted with 'RenderThread Looper POLL_ERROR!' (hwui RenderThread looper epoll error); the next start was fine.
Permission checks log 'granted (one rule: denied: ...)' for BLUETOOTH, INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS and READ/WRITE_CALENDAR: an app is answered granted for permissions a rule marks denied.

launch.evidence: The welcome/login sheet (Google, Facebook, Mobile, Email) rendered over the main tabs after a slow first draw (about a minute on a fresh stage).

region.evidence: JOOX shows 'Sorry, JOOX is not available in this location.' The board's network is outside JOOX's markets; content is region-locked, not a Westlake fault.

google_account_selection.evidence: Google -> Play services' legacy chain (SignInActivity -> GoogleApiActivity -> signin SignInActivity -> AccountPickerActivity). microG offered the test account to JOOX's own live picker (picker_accounts offered=true) and 'Choose an account to continue to JOOX' listed it; selecting it was accepted.

google_sign_in.gap: JOOX also requests https://www.googleapis.com/auth/user.birthday.read. With only the identity scopes granted the broker refused it (scope_not_granted). With the scope added, Play services needed Google's interactive consent (GetTokenActivity -> MinuteMaidActivity) and Google's page answered 'This device isn't Play Protect certified'. Back cancelled cleanly (RESULT_CANCELED to JOOX). Blocked by the board's uncertified status, which stays honest.

facebook_sign_in.gap: Not tried: JOOX is region-locked from the board's network, and the in-app Facebook web view crashed on Duolingo.

otherGaps: First attempt: JOOX's SignInHubActivity finished with RESULT_CANCELED a few seconds after handing off to Play services, so the incoming request was closed before the account picker (no live caller, count=0, addAccount unsupported). The retry from a fresh process did not repeat it; cause open.

One launch died at startup: Tencent FireEye's memory monitor got a null element from File.listFiles() on /proc/<pid>/fd (NPE in UnixFileSystem.resolve), and an ad SDK's handler killed the process. Not repeated in three other launches; cause open.
Play services' web 'Got it' button (MinuteMaid) showed its pressed state but did not act on a tap-channel touch; Back worked.
